Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award
1.

The petitioner aged about 17 years and 7 months is seeking compensation in the wake of Detailed Accident Report(DAR) filed by police corresponding to the investigation carried out in case FIR No.
242/19 U/s 279/337 IPC registered at PS. Narela Industrial Area with regard to Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 06.05.2019 at about 6:40 pm at Shahpur Garhi, Narela, Delhi, involving Maruti Swift Dzire Car bearing registration no. DL1ZC3969 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner.
DAR filed by police, was treated as claim petition under Section 166(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act').

sentences.text: According to DAR, on 06.05.2019, the petitioner was going to Alipur for some work on his Royal Enfield motorcycle bearing registration no. HR14K5739 which was being driven by him at a normal speed on the correct side of road.

At about 6:40 PM, when he reached at Shahpur Garhi,
Narela, Delhi, offending vehicle which was being driven by its driver (respondent no. 1) at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner came from left side of petitioner's vehicle and hit against his vehicle from the back side with a great force, as a result of which, he alongwith motorcycle fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

He was taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi,
where he was medically examined MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 vide MLC No. 2241/19 and on 07.05.2019, he was taken to Max Hospital,
Shalimar Bagh, Delhi for further treatment.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 1 himself and insured with National Insurance Company Ltd /respondent no. 2 during the period in question.
3. In his written statement, the respondent no. 1 i.e. drivercum owner claimed that the accident had not been caused due to his rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
He further claimed that he was having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 2 at the time of accident.
He denied the averments made in the DAR and prayed for its dismissal.

4. In its written statement, the respondent no. 2/insurance company has claimed that the accident had taken place due to sole negligence of petitioner as he was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

On the basis of these averments, it has prayed for dismissal of DAR.
5.

From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 28.09.2019 by my Ld. Predecessor:
1.

Whether the injured Sh. Sahil suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 06.05.2019 at about 6:40 pm near Shahpur Garhi Narela, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS. Narela Industrial Area due to rashness and negligence on the part of the drivercumowner Sh. Ram Kishan who was MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 driving the vehicle bearing registration no. DL1ZC 3969 and insured with National Insurance Co. Ltd.?

OPP. 
2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
3. Relief.
6.
In support of his claim, the petitioner has examined two witnesses i.e. himself as PW1 and PW2 Dr. Ashutosh Gupta and his evidence was closed vide order dated 02.07.2022.

On the other hand,
no evidence was adduced by any of the respondents and RE was closed vide order dated 20.08.2022.
7. I have heard the arguments addressed by ld counsels for the parties.
I have also gone through the record.
My findings on the issues are as under: ISSUE NO. 1.

In his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A), PW1 has deposed on the lines of averments made in the DAR.
He has relied upon the following documents: S.No. Description of documents Remarks 1. Copy of his Aadhaar Card Ex PW1/1 3.

9. During his crossexamination on behalf of respondents no. 1 & 2, he denied the suggestion that accident had not taken place with the offending vehicle or that the respondent no. 1 had stopped the offending vehicle in order to help him or that he had deposed falsely against the respondent no. 1 for securing MACT claim.
During his cross examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that motorcycle Royal Enfield which was being driven by him belonged to his father.
He further deposed that he was not having any driving licence to drive the said motorcycle.
He admitted that he was minor at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that accident had taken place due to his rash and negligent driving.

10. It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that the respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of crossexamination and said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross examination.
Even otherwise, PW1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely about the accident.

Moreover, FIR No. 242/19 (which is part of DAR Ex. PW1/X colly) is shown to have been registered on the MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 statement of petitioner himself.
The contents of said FIR would show that the petitioner has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him as PW1 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.

11. Not only this, the respondent no. 1 namely Sh. Ram Kishan (accused in State case) has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s 279/338 IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

12. Apart from above, copy of MLC (Ex. PW1/2) of injured prepared at SRHC Hospital, Narela,
Delhi, shows that he had been removed to said hospital on 06.05.2019 at about 7:04 pm with alleged history of RTA.
On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned therein.

The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in motor Sh. Sahil Sharma vs Sh. Ram Kishan on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141877707/
3 vehicular accident.

sentences.text: Again, there is no challenge to the said document from the side of respondents including insurance company.

13. The mechanical inspection report dated 09.05.2019 of offending vehicle would show that there were fresh damages on its front MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 side bumper and body; its left side portion was found damaged; its left side grill was found damaged; its bonnet front side middle portion was found dented; its front side number plate was found dented and its front side windscreen glass left side portion was also found broken.

Similarly, mechanical inspection report dated 09.05.2019 of Motorcycle of petitioner would show that there were fresh damages on its rear side wheel left side was damaged; its left side body parts were found scratched; its headlight was found damaged and dislocated; its battery bracket and battery were found dismounted and its left side handle grip end was found scratched.
Both these reports would also corroborate the ocular testimony of the petitioner that the offending vehicle had hit the vehicle of petitioner from back side.

14. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of pre ponderence of probabilities that he had sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 06.05.2019 at about 6:40 pm at Shahpur Garhi, Narela, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE NO. 2.

15. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
MEDICAL EXPENSES 16.

The petitioner deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A) that after the accident, he was removed to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi where he was medically examined vide MLC No.
2241/19 and thereafter, he was taken to Max Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, Delhi, where he remained admitted from 10.05.2019 to 16.05.2019.

He further deposed that he had incurred Rs. 4,00,000/
on his medical treatment.
He has relied upon medical bills and prescriptions Ex. PW1/4(colly).
During his cross examination on behalf of respondents, he denied the suggestion that he had already claimed his medical expenses from the Health Insurance Policy taken by him.

17. It is pertinent to mention here that petitioner has relied upon medical bills (which are part of Ex.
PW1/4 colly) to the tune of Rs. 3,99,193/.
It is quite evident that the respondents have not disputed the authenticity and genuineness of the said medical bills during the course of inquiry.
They have also not led any evidence in rebuttal so as to create any doubt on the genuineness of said bills.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs. 3,99,193/(rounded off) is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

sentences.text: The petitioner has categorically deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/A) that he was giving private tuitions and earning Rs. 20,000/ per month at the time of accident.
He further deposed that due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident, he could not work for long time and as such suffered loss of income.

During his crossexamination on behalf of respondents, he deposed that he had not filed any document to show that he was doing private tuition work and earning Rs.
20,000/ at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that he was not earning Rs. 20,000/ by tuition on the date of accident.
19. Apart from the treatment record Ex. PW1/3, the petitioner has failed to file any other medical treatment record in order to show the exact period upto which he had received the medical treatment.
Nevertheless, it can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
As per the discharge summary of Max Hospital, the petitioner was found to have sustained fracture both bone right side.
Apart from this, he is found to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 61% in relation to his right lower limb.
Thus, appropriate amount should be awarded to him under the head of loss of income.

It is relevant to note here that although, the petitioner has failed to file any document showing the exact period upto which he had received the treatment, however, after considering the nature of injuries and permanent disability sustained by MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 him, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work for a period of 5 months or so.

20. Apart from the bald statement made by petitioner in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A that he was giving private tuition and earning about Rs. 20,000/ per month, no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove his monthly income at the time of accident in question.
It may be noted here that petitioner has filed copy of his 10 th class marksheet (Ex. PW1/5) in respect of his educational qualification.

In view of the aforesaid document Ex. PW1/5, I am of the view that loss of income of the petitioner has to be assessed while taking the income of a Matriculate person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question The minimum wages of a Matriculate person were Rs. 17,508/ per month as on the date of accident which is 06.05.2019.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 87,540/ (Rs. 17,508/ x 5) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.

passed in appeal bearing no. MAC.APP 518/2010 decided on 05.07.12, has held as under: " It is difficult to measure the pain and suffering in terms of money which is suffered by a victim on account of serious injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident.

sentences.text: 22. The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/A) that he had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 61% in relation to his right lower limb.
Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings and mental shock on account of the accident in question.

Keeping in view the medical treatment record of petitioner available on record and the nature of injuries suffered by him, I hereby award a sum of Rs. 75,000/ towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.
LOSS OF GENERAL AMENITIES & ENJOYMENT OF LIFE 23.
As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 61% in relation to his right lower limb.
In the present case, petitioner is a young boy of aged about 18 years at the time of accident.

Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD:
16.02.2023 affected.

In view of the nature of injuries suffered by him, I award a notional sum of Rs.
75,000/ towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 24.
In his evidence, the petitioner has deposed that he had spent a sum of Rs. 50,000/ each on special diet, conveyance and attendant charges.
The petitioner has failed to lead any cogent evidence to prove the amount spent by him under the aforesaid heads.
At the same time, it cannot be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 61% in relation to his right lower limb.

Thus, he would have taken special rich protein diet for his speedy recovery and would have also incurred considerable amount towards conveyance charges while commuting to the concerned hospital as OPD patient for his regular check up & follow up during the period of his medical treatment.
He would have been definitely helped by some person either outsider or from his family, to perform his daily activities as also while visiting the hospital during the course of his medical treatment.

In these facts and circumstances, I hereby award a notional sum of Rs. 15,000/
each for special diet, conveyance and attendant charges to the petitioner.
LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME 25.
As already stated above, the petitioner is shown to have sustained 61% permanent disability in relation to his right lower limb.
Same MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 is quite evident from Disability Certificate dated 22.03.2021 (Ex. PW2/1) of Medical Board of SRHC Hospital, Delhi.

sentences.text: As per the testimony of PW2 Dr. Ashutosh Gupta, who was one of the members of Medical Board constituted at SRHC Hospital, the petitioner was found to have suffered 61% permanent disability in relation to his right lower limb.
He deposed that the aforesaid Medical Board assessed the disability of the patient to be permanent in nature which is not likely to improve.
He exhibited the Disability Certificate as Ex. PW2/1.
He had also brought the calculation chart with disability evaluation details and exhibited the same as Ex. PW2/2.

He deposed that on account of nature and extent of disability sustained by the petitioner, he would have moderate difficulty on walking on plain surface, walking on slope, sitting in crossleg, in kneeling and in taking turns.
He further deposed that petitioner would have very mild difficulty in standing on both legs.
He further deposed that he would also have moderate to severe difficulty in climbing on stairs, standing on affected (right) leg.
On being asked, he categorically deposed that the injured can not be selected in Armed Forces and Police Force under normal general quota but he can do sitting job in any type of services.
During his crossexamination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that the injured can work normally while sitting and doing desk job.
Respondent no. 1 did not crossexamine this witness despite grant of opportunity.
MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 27.

The disability certificate (Ex. PW2/1) of injured would reveal that he had suffered 61%
permanent disability in relation to his right lower limb.
He was giving private tuition at the time of accident which necessarily involves movement of both the lower limbs.
Thus, it would be difficult for him to do the said work with ease or any kind of employment requiring movement of lower limbs or even to do his day to day activities himself.

Taking the overall facts and circumstances of the case,
including the nature of injuries sustained by claimant and the kind of avocation he was doing at the time of accident, his functional disability is taken as 40% in relation to whole body.
28. In copy of 10th class marksheet (Ex. PW1/5) of petitioner, his date of birth is mentioned as 30.12.2001.
The date of accident is 06.05.2019.
Thus, the petitioner was aged about 17 years 7 months as on the date of accident.
Hence, the appropriate multiplier would be 18 in view of judgment passed in case titled as "Sarla Verma Vs. DTC", 2009 ACJ 1298 SC.

sentences.text: After considering the rival submissions made on behalf of both the sides, I find substance in the submissions raised on behalf of petitioner/claimant.
Petitioner is found to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 61% in relation to his right lower limb.
In view of the aforesaid disability suffered by the petitioner, his chances of getting married have definitely been considerably reduced.
He was aged somewhere about 18 years at the time of accident.

It has been established from the disability report that disability suffered by the injured in respect of his right lower limb is likely to continue throughout his life and the same was permanent in nature.
Thus, compensation under the head of loss of marriage prospects also deserves to be awarded in favour of petitioner.
Hence, notional sum of Rs. 50,000/ is awarded to him under this head.

31.
Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

Ld. Counsel for insurance company sought to avoid the liability of insurance company to pay the compensation amount on the ground that there was contributory negligence on part of injured/petitioner who was driving the aforesaid motorcycle without driving licence at the time of accident.
Ld. Counsel for insurance company has placed reliance upon the case titled as "Rehmani Begum & Ors. Vs. Krishan Pal & Ors.", MAC APP No. 954/2017, decided on 18.01.19 by Hon'ble Delhi High Court.

entities.text: Rehmani Begum & Ors. Vs. Krishan Pal & Ors.", MAC APP No. 954/2017
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have gone through the said decision.

However, the said decision is distinguishable in the facts and circumstances of the present case inasmuchas in the said case, the victim MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 was found driving his vehicle under the influence of liquor and had hit a stationary truck from back side while on an extremely fast speed after coming on wrong side of the road, which is not the situation in the present case.
Rather, the offending vehicle had hit the motorcycle of petitioner after coming from from back side.
In this backdrop, the principle of 'resipsa loquitor' would be applicable herein.
Hence, I am of the opinion that no mileage can be derived by insurance company from the above cited decision.

sentences.text: On the other hand, Ld. counsel for petitioner/claimant has vehemently argued that there was no negligence whatsoever on the part of petitioner and thus, the insurance company is liable to pay entire awarded amount to the petitioner.

33. It may be noted that there is no iota of evidence brought on record to show that there was any kind of negligent act on the part of petitioner or that the act of petitioner had contributed in the occurrence of accident in any manner.
Rather, it is established on record from the ocular testimony of PW1 Sh. Sahil that the accident in question had taken place due to sole negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Said portion of his testimony has remained unchallenged and unrebutted from the side of respondents.
Merely because petitioner was not holding DL at the time of accident, would not be sufficient to deduct any amount on account of contributory negligence on his part.

While saying so, I am also MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 fortified by the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case titled as " Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs. Surinder Singh & Ors.", IV (2008) ACC 770 (SC) and Dinesh Kumar J. @ Dinesh J Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd, Civil Appeal No. 22966 of 2017, decided on 15.12.2017.

2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?
14. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of pre ponderence of probabilities that he had sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 06.05.2019 at about 6:40 pm at Shahpur Garhi, Narela, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.
11. Not only this, the respondent no. 1 namely Sh. Ram Kishan (accused in State case) has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s 279/338 IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.
Nevertheless, it can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
As per the discharge summary of Max Hospital, the petitioner was found to have sustained fracture both bone right side.
Apart from this, he is found to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 61% in relation to his right lower limb.
Thus, appropriate amount should be awarded to him under the head of loss of income.
It is relevant to note here that although, the petitioner has failed to file any document showing the exact period upto which he had received the treatment, however, after considering the nature of injuries and permanent disability sustained by MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 him, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work for a period of 5 months or so.
In view of the aforesaid document Ex. PW1/5, I am of the view that loss of income of the petitioner has to be assessed while taking the income of a Matriculate person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question The minimum wages of a Matriculate person were Rs. 17,508/ per month as on the date of accident which is 06.05.2019.
Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the matter titled as " Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors."
passed in appeal bearing no. MAC.APP 518/2010 decided on 05.07.12, has held as under: " It is difficult to measure the pain and suffering in terms of money which is suffered by a victim on account of serious injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident.
Keeping in view the medical treatment record of petitioner available on record and the nature of injuries suffered by him, I hereby award a sum of Rs. 75,000/ towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.
At the same time, it cannot be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Thus, it would be difficult for him to do the said work with ease or any kind of employment requiring movement of lower limbs or even to do his day to day activities himself.
Taking the overall facts and circumstances of the case,
including the nature of injuries sustained by claimant and the kind of avocation he was doing at the time of accident, his functional disability is taken as 40% in relation to whole body.
He was aged somewhere about 18 years at the time of accident.
It has been established from the disability report that disability suffered by the injured in respect of his right lower limb is likely to continue throughout his life and the same was permanent in nature.
Thus, compensation under the head of loss of marriage prospects also deserves to be awarded in favour of petitioner.
Rather, the offending vehicle had hit the motorcycle of petitioner after coming from from back side.
33. It may be noted that there is no iota of evidence brought on record to show that there was any kind of negligent act on the part of petitioner or that the act of petitioner had contributed in the occurrence of accident in any manner.
Rather, it is established on record from the ocular testimony of PW1 Sh. Sahil that the accident in question had taken place due to sole negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Said portion of his testimony has remained unchallenged and unrebutted from the side of respondents.
Merely because petitioner was not holding DL at the time of accident, would not be sufficient to deduct any amount on account of contributory negligence on his part.
While saying so, I am also MACP No. 450/19; FIR No. 242/19; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD: 16.02.2023 fortified by the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case titled as " Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs. Surinder Singh & Ors.", IV (2008) ACC 770 (SC) and Dinesh Kumar J. @ Dinesh J Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd, Civil Appeal No. 22966 of 2017, decided on 15.12.2017.
